evidence: patch 5300: CertSetCRLContextProperty keeps the documented blob properties and the user range (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-certsetcrlcontextproperty lists CERT_FIRST_USER_PROP_ID..CERT_LAST_USER_PROP_ID); crypt32 crl test (check_blob_properties), mutant SG_MUTANT_PROP_USER fails

patch 5300: every certificate property the CertSetCertificateContextProperty page gives a CRYPT_DATA_BLOB or DWORD (ARCHIVED, ARCHIVED_KEY_HASH, CA_DISABLE_CRL, ..., KEY_SPEC) is kept; the ones the page calls 'reserved' stay failing; patch 5301 makes ARCHIVED hide certificates from enumeration (CertOpenStore CERT_STORE_ENUM_ARCHIVED_FLAG text); tests cert.c/store.c, mutants PROP_BLOB, ENUM_ARCHIVED, FIND_SKIPS fail
patch 5300: CertSetCTLContextProperty user range and ARCHIVED (same pages as CRL); crypt32 ctl test; mutant SG_MUTANT_PROP_USER fails

patch 5302: names registered with CryptSetOIDFunctionValue(0,CryptDLLFindLocalizedName,LocalizedNames,...) are searched before the preinstalled ones (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptfindlocalizedname); crypt32 oid test; mutants LOCALIZED_REGISTERED, OIDVALUE_ZERO fail; unverified: encoding-0 Set/Get storage

CertGetPublicKeyLength docs only say 'length of the public/private keys in bits' (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-certgetpublickeylength); for szOID_RSA_DH the key is an INTEGER y with the prime in the algorithm parameters, no Wine test (tests/cert.c 4334-4388 cover RSA/DSA/ECC only) and no page says whether Windows returns bits(p) or bits(y)

the FIXME only fires for CERT_CLOSE_STORE_FORCE_FLAG (CHECK_FLAG is handled since patch 5029): learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-certclosestore says FORCE frees the contexts and may only be used when neither the store nor its contexts are passed on, so keeping them alive here is not observable by a conforming caller

The remaining documented parameters (CMSG_ENCRYPT_PARAM, CMSG_UNPROTECTED_ATTR_PARAM, CMSG_CMS_RECIPIENT_INFO_PARAM, recipient index after decrypt) need data the enveloped model does not keep (unprotected attributes, non-key-transport recipients): see notes 5303

patch 5304: CMSG_VERIFY_SIGNER_CHAIN and CMSG_VERIFY_SIGNER_NULL (CMSG_CTRL_VERIFY_SIGNATURE_EX_PARA page); crypt32 test msg; mutants that wrongly accept (VERIFY_NULL_ACCEPTS, VERIFY_CHAIN_ACCEPTS) fail it

patch 5305: CRYPT_MESSAGE_KEYID_SIGNER_FLAG, BARE_CONTENT_OUT_FLAG, SILENT_KEYSET_FLAG (CRYPT_SIGN_MESSAGE_PARA page); still FIXME: ENCAPSULATED_CONTENT_OUT_FLAG and dwInnerContentType (no CMS encapsulation in CryptMsgOpenToEncode, mapping of the CMSG_* type to an inner OID undocumented); crypt32 test message, mutants SIGN_NO_BARE, SIGN_NO_KEYID fail

patch 5305: CMSG_CTRL_VERIFY_SIGNATURE matches a key-id signer against the CERT_INFO's subject key identifier extension, verified with a real RSA signature in crypt32 test message; mutant SG_MUTANT_KEYID_ANY (accepts any certificate) fails; the matching rule itself is undocumented (notes 5305)

patch 5306: ISSUER_CHAIN (CryptVerifyCertificateSignatureEx page), also ISSUER_NULL for hash signatures (verified against Wine's Windows-made md5SignedEmptyCert), E_INVALIDARG for a hash signature with other issuers, DISABLE_MD2_MD4 flag; mutants that wrongly accept fail the crypt32 cert test; OCSP subject and strong-property flags are not done (formats undocumented)

CryptMsgEncodeAndSignCTL: dwFlags other than 0 is CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CTL_FLAG only (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptmsgsignctl: 'to encode a CMS compatible V3 SignedData message'); that needs the CMS encapsulation of the CTL in an OCTET STRING in CryptMsgOpenToEncode (CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CONTENT_FLAG, absent from msg.c) and the page does not say what the signature covers; no Wine test; producing a message a Windows verifier may reject is worse than failing, so it still fails (FALSE) with the FIXME

CryptMsgSignCTL: same flag, same reason as CryptMsgEncodeAndSignCTL (CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CTL_FLAG needs CMSG_CMS_ENCAPSULATED_CONTENT_FLAG support in the signed-message encoder; the digest coverage for encapsulated content is not documented)
